**Syddanmark** (Region of Southern Denmark) is one of the five administrative regions of [[danmark|Danmark]]. It is systematically monitored within the national Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) to evaluate the quality, safety, and efficiency of acute abdominal surgical care across its hospitals.

### Clinical Quality Indicators
Syddanmark's performance on several key clinical indicators has been a subject of scrutiny due to significant deviations from national standards. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which measures antibiotic treatment within three hours, the region recorded a compliance rate of just 13.5% (95% CI: 10.6–16.9) during the period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023 [^src1]. This was the lowest regional result among the five Danish regions and fell drastically short of the >90% standard [^src1]. In the subsequent reporting period (September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024), the region's compliance improved to 22.5% (95% CI: 19.2–26.0), though it remained low [^src6].

Performance on other indicators also highlights areas requiring targeted resource allocation and process improvements. For [[indikator-5x|Indikator 5x]], an experimental metric tracking surgery within six hours for life-threatening conditions like perforation, ischemia, or bleeding, 37 out of 208 patients in Syddanmark were operated on within the timeframe, yielding a proportion of 17.8% (95% CI: 12.8–23.7) [^src2]. Furthermore, the region recorded the lowest regional fulfillment for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] (early nutritional assessment), with a mere 0.2% (95% CI: 0.0–0.9) compliance rate [^src3]. 

Regarding patient outcomes, 21 out of 213 patients in Syddanmark with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]] died within 30 days following acute surgery, corresponding to a mortality rate of 9.9% (95% CI: 6.2–14.7) [^src4].

### Demographics and Hospitals
Despite the variations in clinical indicator fulfillment, supplementary analyses show that the underlying patient populations do not differ significantly across regions. Specifically, there are no substantial differences between Syddanmark and the other regions—[[hovedstaden|Hovedstaden]], [[midtjylland|Midtjylland]], [[nordjylland|Nordjylland]], and [[sjaelland|Sjælland]]—in terms of patient [[alder|alder]] (age) or [[asa-score|ASA]] score distributions [^src5]. 

The region's acute surgical care is delivered through several monitored facilities, including [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]], [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]], [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]], and [[sygehus-soenderjylland|Sygehus Sønderjylland]] [^src4].

## Claims

**performance**
- For Indikator 1 var andelen i Region Syddanmark i perioden 01.09.2022–31.08.2023 13,5 % (95 % CI: 10,6–16,9) [^src1]

**performance-statistic**
- I Region Syddanmark blev 37 ud af 208 patienter opereret inden for 6 timer for perforation, iskæmi eller blødning, svarende til en andel på 17,8 % (95 % CI: 12,8–23,7) [^src1]

**statistical**
- Region Syddanmark havde den laveste regionale opfyldelse af Indikator 8 med 0,2 % (95 % CI: 0,0–0,9) [^src1]

**regional-statistic**
- Syddanmark: 21 / 213 døde indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi med Charlson Score = 1 eller 2 (9,9 %; 95 % CI: 6,2-14,7) [^src1]

**conclusion**
- Denne supplerende opgørelse viser, at ASA-scoren for de opererede ikke er væsentligt forskellig regionerne imellem [^src1]
- Figuren viser, at der ikke er væsentlig forskel på patienternes alder, regionerne imellem [^src2]

**performance-result**
- For Indikator 1 var opfyldelsen i Region Syddanmark i perioden 01.09.2023–31.08.2024 22,5 % (95 % CI: 19,2–26,0) [^src1]
